about.title: Lake Forest Product Liability Claims
about.longDescription: A product is supposed to do its job without hurting you. When it doesn't — a space heater that catches fire in a Lake Forest garage, a car seat that fails on the I-5, a power tool that kicks back during a weekend project — California law takes a different approach than it does for most injuries. Under strict product liability, you generally do not have to prove the manufacturer was careless. You show the product had a design, manufacturing, or warning defect, and that the defect caused your injury. That shift matters for families across Orange County, because the companies on the other side are usually large and well-prepared. LawProactive is a free service, not a law firm. We connect Lake Forest residents with an independent personal injury attorney who handles defective product claims on contingency, meaning no fee unless there is a recovery. Hold onto the product, the packaging, and any receipts, and reach out when you are ready.

whyChoose.title: Why Lake Forest Residents Use LawProactive

items.title: Strict Liability Changes the Question
items.desc: In California, a defective product case usually turns on whether the product was flawed and caused harm, not on whether the maker was negligent. An attorney who knows this framework can frame your claim accordingly from day one.

items.title: Every Link in the Chain Can Be Responsible
items.desc: Manufacturers, distributors, and the store where you bought the item may all share liability under California law. Identifying each of them early can matter when one company is overseas or out of business.

items.title: The Product Is the Evidence
items.desc: Keeping the failed item, its packaging, and any instructions intact is often the single most important step. We connect you with an independent attorney who can advise on preservation and handles the case on contingency.

items.question: My car's airbag failed to deploy in a crash on El Toro Road. Is that a product liability case or a car accident case?
items.answer: It can be both. Lake Forest recorded 163 injury collisions in 2025, and some crash injuries are made worse by a vehicle component that did not perform as designed. If an airbag, seatbelt, or brake system failed, a product liability claim against the manufacturer may run alongside any claim against another driver. Keep the vehicle from being repaired or scrapped until an attorney has weighed in.

items.question: Do I have to prove the company knew the product was unsafe?
items.answer: Generally, no. California applies strict liability to most defective product claims, so the central questions are whether the product had a design, manufacturing, or warning defect and whether that defect caused your injury. The company's knowledge or carelessness is usually not something you must establish, though it can still be relevant in some situations.

items.question: I threw away the product that hurt me. Do I still have a claim?
items.answer: Possibly, but it is harder, so stop discarding anything else related to the incident now. Photos, receipts, the box, the instruction sheet, and medical records can help fill in the picture. An attorney can also look at recalls, similar complaints, and the retailer's records. Reach out to LawProactive and we will connect you with an independent attorney to review what you have.
